description: We’re a small team from Egypt doing Planet X and SPHEREx. We all love space, and none of us has worked with real telescope data before, so we’re learning it together. We know some Python, data analysis and astronomy, and we like making things look good. What we really need is someone who enjoys writing and presenting, for the slides and the story.
summary: We have created a no-setup 4-page web application called ASTROVITAL (Autonomous Spaceflight Medical Twin, Telemetry & ARED Solutions OS). This includes interactive 6 system anatomical Bio-Twin, Biometric Telemetry (ECG/SpO2 Oscilloscope, Intracranial Pressure, Radiation Dosimetry & Bone Mineral Density), a 30-day Risk Assessment Engine covering NASA R-I-D-G-E spaceflight risks, and interactive NASA ARED vacuum piston and Wolff's Law countermeasure. ASTROVITAL solves this problem by implementing NASA Human Research Program (HRP) and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) medical technologies (e.g., Bio-Monitor Smart Shirt, SANSORI-2) into practical medical decision making. By simulating Lunar, Deep Space Transit, and Martian environments with up to 21min one way delay, crew members without medical training can use the platform to perform step-by-step autonomous triage, simulate emergent problems, and control countermeasures. Humanity are now striving towards going to the Moon and Mars, which due to the vast distances, makes it impossible to provide real-time telemedicine from Earth. ASTROVITAL is essential as it allows crew members to autonomously identify, predict, and counteract dangerous situations that occur during spaceflight such as Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS), cosmic radiation exposure, and bone loss in microgravity to ensure astronauts survive millions of miles away from Earth.
details:
Executive Summary

Astrovital provides a dual source medical telemetry and triage application to help astronauts during isolated space travel. Using a combination of real time data from astronauts’ suits and subjective input from the crew it provides an automatic medical assistant. It uses modern web technologies including HTML/CSS/JavaScript to provide a quick diagnostic tool. This helps astronauts by eliminating the need to wait on mission control on earth.

1. System Architecture and Web Application

The application is a self-contained web application that can be used in isolated deep space environments like Mars, where the communications delay could be up to 44 minutes. Everything is processed on the spacecraft itself.

The application consists of:

app.js/index.html – This is the main dashboard of the application where astronauts inside the spacecraft can monitor any astronauts performing EVA.

data.js/sample_telemetry_seed.json – This contains the data processing for the application. It processes the real time vital signs.

styles.css/tailwind.config.js – This contains the styles for the dashboard. It uses a high contrast futuristic design so the data is easy to read in bright conditions.

2. Two Source Data

Astrovital works using two sources of data:

A. Automatic Data

Modern spacesuits have sensors to monitor vital signs inside the suit. This is automatically sent to Astrovital. This includes:

Oxygen Saturation (SpO₂)

Heart Rate (BPM) and ECG.

Body Temperature

Pressure Inside Suit (PSI)

CO₂ Pressure (mmHg)

B. Manual Data

Sensors cannot pick up on subjective information or any visual trauma. This means astronauts can enter in additional information. This includes:

Pain (1-10)

Paleness, Cyanosis, Bleeding, Confusion

Nausea, Fatigue, Dizziness.

3. Triage

The main functionality of the application is in the triage.js file. This acts as a diagnosis tool. It monitors the two data types to ensure no critical mistakes occur.

It compares the real time data against normal levels. (SpO₂ should be above 95% and the suit pressure should be 4.3 PSI.)

It looks for any critical correlations. If the astronaut has an increased heart rate this may simply be due to exercise however if this is combined with a manual entry from the astronaut reporting they are short of breath and a slight decrease in suit pressure then the risk level increases immediately.

Risks are categorised into categories. This includes:

Nominal

Observation

Warning

Critical.

4. Output and Dashboard

The dashboard has been specifically designed for stressful situations where quick thinking is required.

Live Graphs (charts.js)

This converts the raw numbers into easy to understand graphs and charts. The medical officer or crewmates can see how the vital signs are trending. (Slow increase in body temperature.)

Warnings & Diagnosis

If the triage system detects an issue the dashboard will turn into a warning format. This will include flashing borders and sounds. The system will provide diagnosis solutions. This includes showing what actions should be taken. (E.G: ‘Open O2 bypass valve manually.’) This means even if the person isn’t a medical professional they know what to do in a crisis and can help stabilise their crewmates.
